title: What Happens When You Get Struck By Lightning?

lines.text: A single bolt of lightning contains up to one billion volts, and heats the air to fifty-thousand degrees Fahrenheit.
That is five times hotter than the surface of the Sun. So what happens if it strikes you?
In less than a millisecond, the massive current hits your skin, triggering an effect called an external flashover.
Any sweat or rain on your body instantly flash-boils into steam, expanding so violently it blows your clothes right off.
Metal necklaces, belt buckles, and zippers instantly superheat, welding directly into your skin.
Internally, the colossal electrical surge short-circuits your nervous system, instantly flatlining your heart into cardiac arrest.
As microscopic capillaries rupture, red blood cells bleed into your skin, creating permanent fractal tree scars called Lichtenberg figures.
Yet miraculously, over ninety percent of people actually survive, because the bolt passes in mere microseconds.
